Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, she's always complaining that things look blurry to her. I'm worried it might be affecting her schoolwork or something. We should probably get her eyes checked again soon.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, she had a glue ear last month, and we had to take her to the doctor for antibiotics. It was a real scare, but thankfully, the medicine worked well.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: To be honest, her teeth have been a bit of a nightmare. She needs to go to the dentist every few months for check-ups and fillings because she's prone to cavities. I feel like I'm always taking her somewhere for some dental issue or another.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The cardiologist found something wrong with one of her heart valves. I'm trying to stay on top of the appointments and make sure she takes her medication as prescribed. It's just so worrying as a parent.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: She was diagnosed with hypotonia, which means her muscles are too stiff sometimes. The specialist says it's manageable with therapy and exercise, but I get anxious about her falling or getting hurt because of it.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Eating can be a battle with her; she's very picky and will refuse certain foods. I worry it might affect her growth or overall health if we can't find a balance.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: She has hip dysplasia, which affects her walking and running. And unfortunately, she also has scoliosis. Both conditions require regular monitoring and physical therapy sessions. As a parent, it's heartbreaking to see her deal with these challenges, but we're managing them the best we can.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve issue that requires medication and regular monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties and is a picky eater, which may affect her growth and overall health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which means her muscles are too stiff sometimes, and requires therapy and exercise to manage it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have other neurological issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear last month and has had issues with hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision and may need to have her eyes checked.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has frequent dental issues, including cavities, and needs regular check-ups and fillings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing issues may affect her schoolwork.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often need extra help in school and may require special education plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder and ADHD.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia and scoliosis, which affect her walking and running and require regular monitoring and physical therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and spinal issues.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups and monitoring for the patient's dental issues
* Regular hearing reviews and monitoring for the patient's hearing issues
* Eye exams to monitor the patient's vision and address any concerns
* Cardiac monitoring and medication management for the patient's heart valve issue
* Physical therapy and exercise to manage the patient's hypotonia
* Monitoring and management of the patient's hip dysplasia and scoliosis
* Consideration of referral for endocrine investigations if the patient's growth velocity is a concern
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed

a) How this affects the patient: The patient is a slow gainer when it comes to weight and eats well but doesn't seem to put on weight as quickly as her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets really tired when playing or running around, and it's not just being lazy; she genuinely can't keep up like other kids.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing and often asks for things to be repeated, and she has had trouble with her ears.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things clearly, often squints, and her eyes get tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, people with KBG syndrome can have weak enamel, and regular dental check-ups are important.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Regular dental check-ups and treatments for the patient's teeth
* Regular hearing reviews for the patient
* Eyesight review for the patient
* Cardiac review for the patient
* Consideration of a palate review for the patient
* Referral for a skeletal review for the patient

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a minor heart condition that requires regular check-ups to monitor her condition closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges with food variety and certain textures, making mealtime stressful, and has difficulty with chunky or hard foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems a bit clumsy and uncoordinated, taking more time and effort to complete simple tasks like tying shoelaces or buttoning shirts.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have difficulties with coordination and balance.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets overwhelmed in loud environments and often covers her ears, and has mentioned struggling to see the board during lessons at school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple aeration tube insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has mentioned struggling to see the board during lessons at school, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger front teeth than usual, but otherwise healthy teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, and some may have weak enamel or other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing difficulties may affect her learning, and she may require extra support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is taking a little longer than expected to achieve certain developmental milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common in people with KBG syndrome, and many have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as short fingers, curved fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent any potential issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and provide any necessary corrections or support.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition and provide any necessary treatment or support.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's developmental and behavioural needs.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties with food textures and shows a lack of interest in feeding, which can be a significant and long-lasting issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is not as coordinated as other children, is a bit more clumsy, and has developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have difficulties with coordination and developmental delays.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, as evidenced by not responding to his name being called.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to see the board at school, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble chewing harder foods and has short fingers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing difficulties are making learning challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and is a bit behind other kids.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delays.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has short fingers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers or other skeletal anomalies.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth and chewing difficulties
* Regular hearing reviews to address potential hearing loss

* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and coordination difficulties

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter often squints when she's trying to focus on objects or people, which makes us worry about her eyesight. We've noticed this happening quite frequently, especially when she's reading or watching TV. We're concerned it might affect her performance in school.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, our child gets extremely frustrated in noisy environments. She covers her ears and sometimes even starts crying due to the overwhelming sound levels. This behavior is quite consistent and has been observed by her teachers as well.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth seem very brittle and prone to breaking or chipping. We've had to take extra precautions during meals to avoid any accidents. It's worrying because she loves crunchy foods like apples and carrots.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: During physical activities, her breathing rate increases more rapidly than we expect for a child of her age. While it doesn't stop her from playing or engaging in sports, it's something we monitor closely to ensure it doesn't lead to any complications.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Unfortunately, yes. She experiences seizures occasionally. They're usually triggered by specific factors that we're still working with her doctors to identify and manage. It's been challenging but we're learning to recognize the signs and respond appropriately.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: She has bowel problems. Sometimes she has difficulty passing stool or experiences abdominal pain after eating certain foods. We've been exploring dietary changes to help alleviate these issues.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: One thing that stands out is her noticeable difference in posture when she stands or walks. Her back curves slightly more than typical for a child her age. We're also monitoring this closely as per the advice of her healthcare providers.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing rate during physical activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing rate increases more rapidly than expected during physical activities, suggesting potential cardiac concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems, including difficulty passing stool and abdominal pain after eating certain foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures occasionally, triggered by specific factors that are still being identified and managed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets extremely frustrated in noisy environments, covers her ears, and sometimes cries due to overwhelming sound levels.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on objects or people, which may affect her eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem very brittle and prone to breaking or chipping.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's squinting and potential eyesight issues may affect her performance in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a noticeable difference in posture when standing or walking, with a slightly curved back.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth brittleness and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess and address potential vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental delays and behavioral differences
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord if clinical concerns arise

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve abnormality in her heart that is monitored regularly, which has not caused significant limitations on her daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties due to food texture, which can be a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced developmental delay, with milestones like walking and sitting taking longer than average to achieve. Additionally, the patient has speech struggles with clarity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often turning the television volume up high to hear it comfortably.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which sometimes gives her a cross-eyed appearance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip rather easily, requiring vigilance about what she eats.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences speech struggles and developmental delays, which may impact her educational progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes a bit longer to hit developmental milestones compared to what's typically expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent chipping or breaking.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor hearing difficulties and address any related issues.
* Eyesight review to monitor vision problems and address any related issues.
* Cardiac review to monitor the valve abnormality and address any related issues.
* Speech therapy to address speech struggles and improve clarity.
* Occupational therapy to address feeding difficulties and food texture challenges.
* Consideration of physiotherapy to support developmental progress and address any related issues.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems, which are being managed with increased fiber and water intake.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have feeding difficulties, and a small number may require short-term or long-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily after physical activity and has a unusual gait.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient may have hearing difficulties, as evidenced by delayed response to his name being called.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints and has trouble seeing things clearly, especially when reading or watching TV.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity to cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have weak enamel, large front teeth, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual posture and gait, which may affect his back.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of the spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected when playing, which is noticeable compared to other kids her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than expected when playing, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very picky about what she eats and has issues with food textures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered spinal cord, which is being monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in her ear, which has been mentioned by doctors a few times but hasn't shown much improvement yet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV or books, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with chewing harder foods and tends to avoid them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally behind other children, which has been discussed with her teachers and doctors.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally behind other children.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered spinal cord.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and some have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision problems
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor heart conditions
* Skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor skeletal concerns
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) if clinical concerns arise

consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has astigmatism, which means she has trouble seeing things clearly unless they're really close up. It's been a challenge for her in school when trying to read from the board or watch videos.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes when we call her name, she doesn't respond right away. It's like she's not hearing us even though we know she can because when we get her attention directly she responds just fine. This has been a bit concerning for us as parents.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her front teeth are noticeably larger than what you'd expect for a child her age. We've had comments from other parents and teachers about it and we're planning to consult an orthodontist soon to see if there's anything that needs to be done.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: During playtime or when she's running around with friends, her breathing gets faster sooner than the other kids. At first we thought maybe she was just more excited or less fit, but it's happened enough times now that we're starting to wonder if everything is okay with her heart.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: She seems less coordinated compared to her peers. Simple tasks like tying shoelaces or climbing on the playground equipment take her longer to figure out and sometimes end in falls or mishaps. It's worrying to see her struggle with balance and overall movement skills.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Mealtimes have become a real challenge for our daughter. Some days are better than others but frequently she experiences discomfort after eating or has trouble digesting certain foods. This has led to avoiding certain meals altogether which worries us about her getting all the nutrients she needs.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: One thing we've noticed is her posture. When she stands or walks it's noticeably different from other children her age. It might sound minor but combined with the coordination issues it makes us concerned there could be something more going on that we should investigate further.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing during playtime or when running around, suggesting potential respiratory or cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's faster breathing during physical activity may indicate a heart condition, and further evaluation is needed to determine the cause.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences discomfort after eating and has trouble digesting certain foods, leading to mealtime challenges and potential nutritional deficiencies.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, balance problems, and difficulty with simple tasks, suggesting potential neurological concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often experience developmental delay, and some may have seizures, with approximately 20-40% of individuals reported to have seizures.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing concerns, as she sometimes doesn't respond to her name being called, suggesting potential hearing loss or auditory processing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects her ability to see things clearly unless they are close up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than expected for her age, and her parents are planning to consult an orthodontist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing concerns may impact her ability to learn and participate in school activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's coordination issues, balance problems, and difficulty with simple tasks may impact her development and behavior.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often experience developmental delay, and some may have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeable posture differences and coordination issues, suggesting potential skeletal concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased risk of scoliosis.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth growth and address any dental concerns
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to assess for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess for heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for skeletal anomalies
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental and coordination concerns
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of referral for specialist review (e.g., orthodontist, cardiologist, ophthalmologist) as needed

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that was identified during a visit to the cardiologist, and regular check-ups are necessary to ensure everything is okay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is managed through diet and exercise, and sometimes requires a little extra help.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures occasionally, which are controlled with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with otitis media and experiences ear infections, which affect his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on things, which makes his parents worry about his eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than expected for his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems behind other kids his age in terms of overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's posture when standing or walking is quite different from what is seen in other children, and he seems behind other kids his age in terms of overall development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have learning difficulties.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's posture when standing or walking is quite different from what is seen in other children.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth development and enamel health.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions.
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal anomalies.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and manage behavioral differences.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart check-ups, indicating potential concerns with heart health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had trouble feeding as a baby, which required time to figure out the best feeding approach.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences moments where she stares off into space and doesn't seem to respond to her surroundings, suggesting potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have difficulty with speech development and learning.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond to her name being called, suggesting potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs her eyes frequently when trying to focus, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups due to concerns about her teeth health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome experience dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school and may need to attend special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to get her words out when trying to talk, indicating potential speech development issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often experience developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome experience skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor teeth health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address potential hearing concerns
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health
* Consideration of a palate review, particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns
* Referral for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental and learning difficulties
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, characterized by muscles that seem too relaxed, affecting her movements and posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often turning the TV volume up high, indicating potential hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism and wears glasses, though consistency in wearing them is a challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, requiring frequent dentist visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have weak enamel and may experience a variety of dental concerns, including large front teeth.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes longer to reach milestones than expected and moves differently compared to other kids her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but possibly requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans for secondary school.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's developmental delay and differences in movement and posture are areas of concern.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage symptoms.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, I'm so worried about his eyes. He often squints when looking at things, and I fear it might affect his vision in the long run. I've tried to get him to wear glasses, but he doesn't like them. I just want to make sure he can see properly.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes... he's had a glue ear before. It was such a scary time for me as a parent. The doctor said it was due to a buildup of fluid and gave us some medication to clear it up. Thankfully‚ it worked‚ and his hearing seems fine now.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth... they break or chip so easily. I'm always on edge when he's eating anything hard‚ fearing he'll hurt himself. We've had to take him to the dentist a few times already‚ and it's just heartbreaking to see him in pain.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The most worrying thing for me is the septal defect in his heart. The thought of my child having to undergo surgery is just terrifying. But the doctors say it's manageable with medication for now‚ and we're closely monitoring the situation.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He has epilepsy. Seeing him have a seizure is just the worst feeling as a parent. We have to be so careful all the time‚ making sure he's safe and the right medication is always nearby.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: When he was a baby‚ feeding was a nightmare. He just wouldn't latch on properly‚ and it took us months to figure out the right formula. Even now‚ he's a bit picky with food‚ but at least he's eating something.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: My biggest concern right now is that he's not speaking as much as other children his age. I know every child develops at their own pace‚ but it's hard not to worry when you see others chatting away and your child is still struggling to find the words.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to get tired more easily than peers, suggesting possible cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences discomfort after meals and has challenges with eating certain foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common, and some individuals require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are managed with neurologists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient occasionally does not respond immediately when called, suggesting possible hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, requiring glasses to correct vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has various dental issues, requiring frequent dentist visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with some requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with hip dysplasia and has shorter fingers than typical.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine, and short fingers with curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect any hearing problems.
* Eyesight review to correct any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess heart condition.
* Consider skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor skeletal development.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage symptoms.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, with weaker muscles than her peers, and has speech difficulties, including not speaking as much as other kids her age and sometimes being hard to understand.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and many have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media in the past and experiences ear infections more often than average, which can cause conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint, which can make her eye alignment seem off sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth require a lot of maintenance, with frequent dentist visits due to cavities and sensitivity issues.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences trance-like states where he stares off into space without responding to external stimuli, and these episodes seem to happen randomly without an identifiable trigger.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has selective hearing, where he can hear certain sounds immediately but doesn't respond to others, such as his name being called from a few feet away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences blurry vision, particularly when trying to focus on distant objects or read from a whiteboard, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than his peers, which has been a point of discussion among the family and friends, and may have potential health implications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, people with KBG syndrome can have weak enamel, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school, but some requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans due to the extra demands of mainstream secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate in certain circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has undescended testicles and a diagnosis of hip dysplasia, which required surgical intervention to correct the alignment of his hip joint.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number having hip dysplasia.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and address any potential issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing and address any potential issues.
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and address any potential issues.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess the patient's heart health and address any potential issues.
* Monitoring of the patient's growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any potential issues.
* Regular monitoring of the patient's testicles and referral for specialist review if there are any concerns.
* Consideration of review and investigation for tethered cord if there are any clinical concerns.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily, such as when playing outside or running around, suggesting possible cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky about food and there are some things she just won't eat.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and experiences fits sometimes, for which she needs to take medicine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't answer when called, suggesting possible hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can see far-away things better than things close up, indicating hypermetropia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to go to the dentist often for extra care, as her teeth need extra attention to prevent them from getting worse.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient doesn't talk as much as she should for her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, and the degree of delay ranges from mild to severe, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as typical children, and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's soft spot on the head took a long time to close.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage the patient's dental health.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for any hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and manage any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess for any heart conditions.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and manage any related issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son has a tendency to squint, which can make it difficult for him to see things clearly, especially when reading or watching television. We've been monitoring this closely and considering corrective measures if necessary.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: He gets overwhelmed in loud environments, which can lead to frustration. However, his hearing itself appears to be within normal ranges, and he responds well to sounds and voices.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth are somewhat brittle and prone to breaking or chipping easily. This has led to several visits to the dentist for repairs and preventive care to ensure his dental health remains good.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Unfortunately, our child was born with a septal defect that requires periodic monitoring and check-ups with cardiologists to ensure it doesn't affect his overall health and development.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, he's been slower to achieve certain milestones such as walking or sitting compared to his peers. This has required closer observation and support from healthcare professionals to address any potential delays or challenges.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been a challenge for our son. He experiences difficulties that have necessitated specialized dietary advice and strategies to manage mealtimes and ensure proper nutrition.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the mentioned issues, another concern is the undescended testes. The medical team is keeping a close watch on these to determine the best course of action and ensure they don't pose additional risks to his health.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that requires periodic monitoring and check-ups with cardiologists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulties with feeding, necessitating specialized dietary advice and strategies to manage mealtimes and ensure proper nutrition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, achieving certain milestones such as walking or sitting slower than peers, and requires closer observation and support from healthcare professionals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets overwhelmed in loud environments and has a tendency to squint, which can make it difficult for him to see things clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple aeration tube insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to squint, which can make it difficult for him to see things clearly, especially when reading or watching television.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are somewhat brittle and prone to breaking or chipping easily, requiring several visits to the dentist for repairs and preventive care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and requires closer observation and support from healthcare professionals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental health concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Consider a palate review, particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns
* Referral for a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences.
