consultation:
Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... her eyes. She has hypermetropia, which means she's very far-sighted. It's been a challenge correcting it, but we're working on it. I worry about her falling or bumping into things because she can't see them coming.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Poor thing, she's had otitis media a few times already. We have to be super careful about ear infections and make sure she gets treated right away if it happens again. I get so worried it might affect her hearing in the long run.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth... they break or chip so easily. It's like they're made of glass or something. We have to watch what she eats and make sure she doesn't bite on anything too hard. I'm always on edge she'll hurt herself.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Well... she can't keep up with the other kids when they play. If they're running around, she gets tired really quickly and needs to sit down. It worries me that there might be something wrong with her heart that we don't know about yet.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally... she was slower to walk and sit up compared to other babies. We were so scared something was seriously wrong, but the doctors said we just had to give her time. Still, I notice she takes longer to learn new things than her friends do.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Mealtimes are... a nightmare. She's very picky and will only eat certain foods. Some days are better than others, but it's always a battle to get her to eat properly. And when she does eat... well, let's just say bowel movements can be a bit unpredictable.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Speech... it's another thing. She struggles to get her words out clearly. You can tell she wants to say something, but it doesn't always come out right. It breaks my heart seeing her try so hard and not being understood.
report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences fatigue quickly, especially when engaging in physical activities like running, which raises concerns about potential heart issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, is very picky, and experiences unpredictable bowel movements, making mealtimes challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding, with a few needing longer-term tube feeding due to lack of interest in feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was developmentally delayed, taking longer to walk and sit up, and currently takes longer to learn new things compared to peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe, with most children eventually acquiring skills but at a delayed pace.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media several times, requiring careful management to prevent hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia (far-sightedness), which is being corrected, but poses challenges, such as increased risk of falls or bumping into objects due to reduced vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are prone to breaking or chipping easily, requiring careful monitoring of diet and activities to prevent damage.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals often have large front teeth and may experience weak enamel, necessitating regular dental check-ups and careful brushing.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's learning pace is slower than peers, which may impact educational progress and require additional support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Most children with KBG syndrome require extra help in school, with some attending mainstream schools and others benefiting from special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences speech difficulties, struggling to articulate words clearly, which can be distressing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often exhibit behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, which may require medication or therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual spinal structure, short fingers (brachydactyly), and curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly), with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent damage.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in early childhood, to address conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct vision problems.
* Consideration of cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess heart condition.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if growth is significantly delayed.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental and behavioural challenges.
* Regular monitoring for signs of tethered cord, especially if sacral dimple is present or if there are concerns about pain, weakness, or unusual gait.
